weakness.title: Use of Cloneable Physical Access Credentials
weakness.description: The facility relies on physical access credentials that can be copied, so a duplicate is accepted as the original.

extended_description.applicability: Credentials that open entry controls, whether electronic (cards, tags, fobs) or mechanical (keys). The protection required depends on the sensitivity of the area. The weakness is the choice or deployment of a credential that can be copied. Flaws in a specific product belong to CWE.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person obtains a copy of a credential, from its holder or from the credential itself, and uses the copy to enter. The entry control cannot tell the copy from the original.

row.details: Copies pass the entry control as valid credentials.
Unauthorized persons reach information, media and equipment.
Entries made with a copy are attributed to the legitimate holder.
A copy stays usable until the original is withdrawn, and its holder may never learn of it.

row.description: Choose credentials that prove their identity cryptographically and cannot be read out in a reusable form, suited to the sensitivity of the area.

row.measure: Replace credential types known to be copyable
row.description: Retire credential technologies that are known to be copied easily.

row.measure: Add a second factor for sensitive areas
row.description: Combine the credential with a PIN or a biometric check for the most sensitive areas.
Use restricted key blanks and record each key issued, so that keys cannot be duplicated without authorization.
Raise an alert when the same credential is used in two places at once, or in an impossible sequence.
Biometric data is sensitive personal data and its use is regulated. Process it in accordance with applicable law.
A second factor must remain usable by persons with disabilities.

row.reference: CAPEC-396: Bypassing Card and Biometric Readers
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control
